lesson.child_mission: Meetings of cultures during early contact involved different languages, laws, technologies and ideas about land. Respectful study names that both First Nations Peoples and visitors brought knowledge, and that contact had many different outcomes depending on place and time.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Rewrite this biased sentence respectfully: “Explorers brought civilisation to empty land.”

FEEDBACK
e.g. “Visitors arrived in lands already cared for by First Nations Peoples, bringing different technologies and ideas; contact had complex effects.”

WATCH FOR
Calling one culture civilised and another primitive is disrespectful and historically false as a ranking.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Complete a two-column “knowledge each group brought” table using published sources only. Write one respectful summary sentence and one limit of the European written record.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Complete a two-column “knowledge each group brought” table using published sources only. Write one respectful summary sentence and one limit of the European written record. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: e.g. “Visitors arrived in lands already cared for by First Nations Peoples, bringing different technologies and ideas; contact had complex effects.” Reasoning: I used contact by attending to culture rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Calling one culture civilised and another primitive is disrespectful and historically false as a ranking. Correction: e.g. “Visitors arrived in lands already cared for by First Nations Peoples, bringing different technologies and ideas; contact had complex effects.” Why: the correction restores accurate use of contact.

Parent: Likely misconception: Calling one culture civilised and another primitive is disrespectful and historically false as a ranking. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating contact on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with contact, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..
